core_obligations: Reduce to showing affineness, which then gives representability by schemes by the locality criterion (proof lines 4215-4217).
Write both spaces as filtered colimits of affine schemes and let a morphism from an affine scheme into the target be given; factor it through a stage of the target (proof lines 4218-4229).

Use quasi-compactness of the morphism to see that the fibre product is quasi-compact and hence that its projection to the source factors through a stage of the source, increasing the stage of the target if necessary (proof lines 4229-4234).
Identify the fibre product with the fibre product of two affine schemes and conclude that it is affine (proof lines 4234-4236).
proof_roadmap: Presentations and the first factorisation (proof lines 4218-4229).
Quasi-compactness and the second factorisation (proof lines 4229-4234).
Identification with a fibre product of affine schemes (proof lines 4234-4236).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable by algebraic spaces is in fact representable by schemes and affine (statement lines 4208-4213). The proof shows affineness by testing against morphisms from affine schemes: both the source and the target are written as filtered colimits of affine schemes, a morphism from an affine scheme into the target factors through one of its stages, quasi-compactness of the morphism makes the fibre product quasi-compact so that the projection to the source factors through one of its stages, and after increasing the chosen stage of the target the fibre product is identified with a fibre product of affine schemes, hence is affine (proof lines 4215-4236). Representability by schemes then follows from the locality criterion for affineness (proof lines 4215-4217). The claim is H2: the argument is a sequence of factorisations through stages, each justified by a named statement, ending in the identification of the fibre product with the fibre product of two affine schemes.
